subject: english-language
source_note: Topic structure follows the National Curriculum KS3 programme of study for English. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Reading
units.blurb: Reading widely, understanding and responding critically to texts

units.name: Writing
units.blurb: Writing accurately and effectively for different purposes and audiences

units.name: Grammar & Vocabulary
units.blurb: Building grammatical knowledge, vocabulary and Standard English

units.name: Spoken English
units.blurb: Speaking, presenting, debating and performing confidently

topics.blurb: A wide range of fiction and non-fiction, pre-1914 and contemporary, Shakespeare and world literature

topics.name: Choosing & Rereading Books
topics.blurb: Reading independently for enjoyment and rereading to compare

topics.name: Inference & Evidence

topics.name: Purpose, Audience & Context
topics.blurb: How purpose, audience and context shape meaning in a text

topics.name: Reading Critically
topics.blurb: How language, structure and form present meaning

topics.name: Poetry & Poetic Conventions
topics.blurb: Recognising poetic conventions and their effects

topics.name: Setting, Plot & Characterisation
topics.blurb: Studying narrative craft and its effects on the reader

topics.name: Drama & Performance
topics.blurb: How drama is communicated in performance and through staging

topics.name: Comparing Texts & Authors
topics.blurb: Critical comparisons across texts and authors studied in depth

topics.name: Writing for Purpose & Audience
topics.blurb: Essays, narrative, scripts, poetry, arguments and letters

topics.name: Summarising & Organising

topics.name: Applying Vocabulary & Grammar

topics.name: Literary & Rhetorical Devices

topics.name: Grammar for Effect

topics.blurb: Discussing language with precise technical vocabulary

topics.blurb: Giving short speeches and keeping to the point

topics.name: Debate & Structured Discussion
topics.blurb: Formal debate, summarising and building on others' ideas

topics.name: Performing Scripts & Poetry

connections.why: Reading widely exposes pupils to the harder vocabulary and ideas they then learn to decode
Securing literal comprehension is the basis for reading between the lines with evidence
Knowing a text's purpose and audience reveals why its language and structure work as they do
Critical reading of language and structure extends naturally to recognising poetic conventions
Analysing how language presents meaning underpins the study of plot and characterisation
Understanding character and plot prepares pupils to read how drama works in performance
Comparing texts critically depends on inferring meaning and citing evidence from each
Noticing devices as a reader is what lets pupils deploy them as writers
Awareness of purpose and audience in reading transfers directly into writing for purpose and audience
Sustained writing needs material to be summarised and organised coherently
Organised ideas are realised by selecting the appropriate form, vocabulary and grammar
Knowing devices feeds the vocabulary and structural choices pupils apply in writing
Drafting is where knowledge of grammar and structure is revised for coherence
Editing and proofreading are when accurate grammar, punctuation and spelling are secured
Analysing grammar in texts shows pupils how to use grammatical features for their own effects
Grammatical analysis is a core tool of critical reading
Conscious control of grammar for effect is applied directly in pupils' writing
Understanding registers and varieties clarifies when and how to use Standard English
Confident Standard English is required across formal and informal spoken contexts
Precise terminology lets pupils articulate critical readings of texts
Effective speaking underpins formal debate and structured discussion
Skills of delivery and impact transfer from presentations to performing scripts and poetry
